notes: Process bounds require explicit annual-to-hourly approval before any hourly use.
Strong conversion coefficients are reviewable earlier than high-risk capacities but still need reviewer approval.
Store capacities are high-risk and should not be promoted early.
Initial inventories should follow reviewed policy logic rather than silent quantity assumptions.
Terminal inventory rules must stay separate from exact terminal quantities.
Production targets should be reviewed late because basis choice changes feasibility and economics.
Validation targets may be reviewed as anchors but may not become constraints without reclassification.
CYC50 may be reviewed as endpoint-policy logic without approving capacities.
Reporting rows are governance rows and do not create executable model behaviour.
Annual public anchors remain non-hourly until explicit translation approval is recorded.
Source cards are mandatory for later promotion review.
Promotion requires compliance with the shared unit and sign conventions.
Every promoted row must state whether it applies to C0 and or C1.
C1S remains an overlay within C1.
C2 may be reviewed only as optional later exogenous hydrogen sensitivity metadata.
Codex may assist review but may not decide which rows become approved inputs.
Promotion decision records must be retained for approval and for rejection or deferral.
Approval and executable status remain separate gates for every category.
